issues.legal_issue: An amendment to correct the valuation of the subject matter of a suit should be allowed when it does not change the nature of the suit or cause irremediable prejudice to the opposing party.
material_facts: The plaintiff brought a suit for specific performance and initially stated a value for the property that it later acknowledged was incorrect.
The plaintiff applied to amend the plaint to state the property's correct market value and offered to pay the additional court fee.
The defendant had itself alleged in its written statement that the plaintiff had undervalued the property.
The amendment would not change the nature of the suit, and no prejudice to the defendant that could not be compensated was identified.
The lower courts rejected the amendment in part because the increased valuation would result in the suit being transferred to the High Court.
issues.conclusion: The amendment should have been allowed. The orders rejecting it were set aside, and the trial court was directed to permit the plaintiff to amend the plaint. The transfer of the suit resulting from the increased valuation was not a valid reason to refuse the amendment.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 6 Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, amendments are generally to be allowed unless they change the nature of the suit or cause prejudice to the opposing party. As stated in North Eastern Railway Administration, Gorakhpur v. Bhagwan Das (D) by LRs. (2008) 8 SCC 511, relying on Pirgonda Hongonda Patil v. Kalgonda Shidgonda Patil (1957) 1 SCR 595, amendments should be allowed when they do not work injustice and are necessary to determine the real questions in controversy; refusal is warranted where the opposing party cannot be restored to its original position and would suffer injury that cannot be compensated in costs. Transfer of the suit because of the amended valuation is not, by itself, a reason to refuse amendment.

rule.if: pleading_amendment_application and seeks_correct_property_valuation and nature_of_suit_unchanged and no_irremediable_prejudice

predicates.pleading_amendment_application: A party to a civil suit applied to amend a pleading.
predicates.seeks_correct_property_valuation: The applying party sought to replace an incorrect valuation of the property with its correct market value.
predicates.nature_of_suit_unchanged: The proposed amendment would leave the nature of the suit unchanged.
predicates.no_irremediable_prejudice: The opposing party would not suffer prejudice that could not be remedied, including by an award of costs.

issues.definition: When a party seeks to amend a pleading to correct a property's valuation without changing the nature of the suit or causing irremediable prejudice to the opposing party, the amendment is allowed.
